organization.description:
**As of August 2025, this page is no longer actively maintained or updated. Sorry for any inconvenience caused. For the latest disaster alerts please visit: https://adam.geospatial.wfp.org/live**

WFP's corporate geospatial solution for emergency preparedness, early warning & response.

Automated Disaster Analysis and Mapping (ADAM) is an operational system for collecting, analysing and mapping geospatial and socio-economic information following sudden onset humanitarian emergencies. Currently operational for floods, earthquakes and tropical storms, ADAM issues alerts and response dashboards aggregating relevant, evidence-based, near-real time risk and impact information. More WFP data can be found here: https://data.humdata.org/organization/wfp

results.name: gdacs-rss-information
results.notes: GDACS alerts are issued for earthquakes and possible subsequent tsunamis, tropical cyclones, floods and volcanoes. Earthquake, tsunami and tropical cyclones calculations and assessments are done automatically, without human intervention. Floods and volcanic eruptions are currently manually introduced. Research and development is continuous to improve the global monitoring.

results.caveats:
•	Data are based on rapid assessments and may not capture all hazards or long-term risks due to time and resource constraints.
•	The information is preliminary and intended for initial emergency response; detailed site-specific investigations should follow.
•	Some data may be incomplete or rely on remote or secondary sources, especially where access was limited.
•	Hazard identification and risk prioritization reflect the situation during the assessment; conditions may change with follow-up monitoring.
•	FEAT tables focus on acute chemical and environmental risks and may not address all chronic or indirect impacts.
•	Methodology relies on standardized assumptions; local context and expert input are recommended for interpretation.
•	Use caution when applying findings to areas outside the original geographic or temporal scope.
results.name: flash-environmental-assessment-tool-feat-tables-12-countries
results.notes:
This tables presents results from the Flash Environmental Assessment Tool assessments conducted in 12 countries in Latin America in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022.

The FEAT helps to identify potential hazards posed by hazardous operations. The FEAT is used at the onset of hazardous operations or disasters, by international humanitarian responders that may be unfamiliar with the affected area.

The FEAT was initially developed based on lessons stemming from the 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake and Tsunami, with the aim to provide a standardized, scientific assessment methodology to prioritize the impacts of chemical accidents following large scale, sudden onset natural disasters.

The outcome of the FEAT is the identification of impact zones (areas most at risk from hazardous chemical releases). These zones highlight locations where urgent response actions are needed to protect human health and the environment.

[More information on the FEAT Tool](https://www.unocha.org/publications/report/world/flash-environmental-assessment-tool-feat-20-pocket-guide)
